title: Lithuania converts a Spike LR2 contract into reported warehouse receipt before stockpile readiness or deterrence is visible
source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of Spike LR2 missile receipt
geography: Lithuania; Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses and Vilkas Infantry Fighting Vehicle force

receipt_stage.value: Spike LR2 missiles reported to have reached Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses

contract_value.unit: euros; more than this amount reported for the implemented Euro Spike GmbH contract

platform_link.value: the ministry says Lithuanian Armed Forces use Spike LR2 missiles with Vilkas Infantry Fighting Vehicles

stated_function.value: rapid-response anti-armour missile effective against tanks, armoured equipment, buildings, and other high-value targets

readiness_and_effect.unit: missing quantity, acceptance, allocation, payment, training, maintenance, firing readiness, field use, replenishment, deterrence, adversary response, civilian protection, and public judgment

mechanism.value: A warehouse receipt converts an implemented ammunition contract into reported possession linked to an existing vehicle platform, but possession is not trained, sustained, or demonstrated operational capability.

observations.method: Structured extraction from the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence announcement. Receipt, contract value, supplier, platform link, stated function, and unmeasured readiness and effects are coded as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not disclose missile quantity, lot, acceptance records, inventory allocation, payment status, crew training, maintenance, firing readiness, field deployment, operational use, or strategic effect.
observations.subgroup: Lithuanian Armed Forces and Vilkas crews, Euro Spike GmbH and defense suppliers, allied defense institutions, and civilians potentially affected by future use; no affected-person denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A replenished stockpile may improve future readiness and platform availability, while stored missiles can remain unused or create fiscal, maintenance, escalation, and civilian-risk costs not measured by the announcement.

related_sources.claim: A separate March 2026 announcement reports an earlier combined AMRAAM, Spike LR2, and ammunition receipt; it is background and not merged into this July receipt milestone.

boundary: This record establishes a reported July 2026 Spike LR2 warehouse receipt, an implemented contract valued above €3 million, and a platform link to Vilkas vehicles. It does not establish quantity, acceptance, training, maintenance, readiness, use, replenishment, deterrence, civilian protection, or public legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project follow-up memo derived from the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence source; contract files, inventory records, training logs, and operational-use data are not retained.
